matches.quote: The Tc(p) fit that sets the headline pc has the wrong sign, an unjustified form and no uncertainty. ... The exponent is not motivated
these data are equally consistent with ... a phase with strongly reduced intralayer exchange.
No calculation supports the abstract's statement that the P-3m1 / A-A phase "becomes stable" under pressure. ... compute the enthalpy H = E + pV
The intralayer J1 to J3 are fixed at ambient-pressure values from Ref. 73 ... redo the simulations with ... pressure-dependent J1 to J3 and JL
The Fig. 4 caption is garbled ("a) ambient pressure, and a) a lower b) and c) lower than the transition temperature")
most of the magnetic suppression happens with no measured change in phase fraction. ... plot Tc and Ms against the measured AA fraction rather than against pressure
Fig. 1 gives the field as 0.1 T in the caption, while the panel says 0.01 T and Fig. 3 says 100 Oe; please correct it
The novelty claim, "first direct experimental evidence" of pressure-induced suppression, should be qualified relative to Refs. 18, 20 and 39, which already measured a decrease of Tc
measure M(T) and M(H) at ambient pressure ... on deliberately cut or deformed crystals with known P-3m1 fractions, to test whether Tc scales with the fault fraction
plot Tc and Ms against the measured AA fraction rather than against pressure ... give error bars on Ms or normalized curves from a single sample
The method for deriving the R-3 fraction in Fig. 5b is not given. The authors should explain whether it comes from the ratio of satellite to main reflections
explain physically how AFM interlayer coupling on some interfaces could drive Tc toward zero ... redo the simulations with ... pressure-dependent J1 to J3 and JL
In this average structure the in-plane √3×√3 honeycomb order is averaged away ... decide between ordered A-A, random stacking and in-plane disorder
The definition of Tc from the 0.01 T M(T) curves (onset, inflection, dM/dT minimum) is not given.
The magnetic pc (6.5 GPa at low T), the XRD transition (6.4 to 8.4 GPa at RT) and the Raman pc (~10 GPa at RT) are quoted together
AA and AB "atoms" are distributed at random site by site (p. 16), whereas stacking faults are a property of whole layer interfaces
Because the starting phase fraction varies by crystal ... list which batch, crystal and run each curve in Figs. 1 to 3 comes from, with its initial phase fraction
state which ordered supercell was used in DFT for "the AA phase" and how the fractional-occupancy structure was mapped onto it

notes: The referees reviewed a version with different figure numbering where the M(T) curves (now Fig. 1) were in Fig. S1; thus C2 (moving magnetization data from Fig. S1 to the main manuscript) and C6 (stating room temperature for Raman, p. 4) are already fixed in arXiv v1, while C4 (Fig. S1 field discrepancy) and C7 (Fig. 2 caption) correspond to Fig. 1 and Fig. 4 in v1. For C10, v1 includes Fig. 5b (R-3 fraction vs. pressure), but without explaining how it was derived from the XRD data or quantifying AA stacking, which P1, P14 and P19 raise. For C8, P18 and P27 raise reduced/pressure-dependent intralayer exchange J1-J3 under compression but do not cite Webster & Yan's monolayer strain prediction, so it is marked partly.
